args.goal: Under a valid lease, turn the existing supplier-to-Shopify comparison prototype into one buyer-readable example of a recurring catalogue update decision. Check for equivalent committed work first and reuse it if present. Otherwise read the documented comparison rules and one existing fictional fixture. Use the existing checker offline on a small fictional update that contains one intended change, one unintended change and one ambiguous duplicate. Save a concise EN/FR report showing the intended change to keep, the unintended change to correct and the duplicate to resolve manually. Tie each recommendation to actual observed output. If the checker cannot make a distinction, identify the human decision and the input it requires. Save reproducible commands and actual output. Use the result to define the inputs and output of a single commissioned update review, with a clear boundary around what the free checker already does. If the worked report adds no concrete decision value, reuse the free example and close on that evidence. Do not invent buyer interest or promise platform import compatibility. Read committed results before closure and record what worked, failed and should change. No external send, new account, spending or deployment. Any later public revision requires host-enforced independent review of its exact digest.
